title: Critical: smart-routing/fallback logic misroutes requests to incorrect model/region/tier
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private/VPC deployments) reported requests being routed to the wrong model variants, wrong region endpoints, or incorrect service tier during peak load. This caused degraded quality, rate-limit errors from incompatible tiers, and customer-facing failures in production. The issue appears tied to a regression in the new fallback policy selector that was merged as part of runtime-2.0.0 scheduling optimizations.

Scope: Affects smart-routing decision path in the control plane used by Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Misroutes observed: (1) Hosted requests pinned to model-v1 were routed to model-v2-quant in a different region, (2) Dedicated requests with reserved tier were routed to a burst pool without quota checks causing 429s, (3) Private customers behind VPC saw calls routed to control-plane-only proxies resulting in 503s.

Immediate customer impact: multiple escalations opened by three customers between 2026-03-11 and 2026-03-12. Two production incidents required rollbacks or manual route pins. SLA violations recorded for Dedicated customers (latency and error budget breaches).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a routing policy that prefers region=A, model family=redwood-std, tier=reserved and set fallback order to [reserved -> burst -> hosted].
2) Generate concurrent requests matching production traffic pattern (many short chat completions + token streaming) to trigger fallback logic under simulated capacity pressure.
3) Observe routing audit logs: control-plane assigns route to model variant in region=B and to burst tier even when reserved capacity is available in region=A.
4) Reproduce in Dedicated and Private staging clusters; reproduce rate-limit 429s for Dedicated after misroute to burst pool.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-11 22:40 UTC we received first customer report of hallucination/regression. By 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC, three customers reported behavioral regressions and increased 429/503 errors. Engineering created a hotfix branch and rolled back the fallback-selector change for the control plane at 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC which mitigated new misroutes. Root cause identified in fallback policy comparator: stale 'compatibility matrix' cache + incorrect priority tie-break for cross-region picks introduced in commit 9f2b3da (PR #4823).
root_cause_analysis: The fallback policy comparator merges three factors: model compatibility, region affinity score, and tier quota availability. A refactor intended to optimize for latency moved the compatibility check after region scoring, and a cache invalidation bug meant the compatibility matrix was stale for up to 10 minutes under high churn.
When compatibility data was stale, the comparator could not detect model incompatibility in the candidate pool and relied on region/tier heuristics, causing cross-region and tier misroutes.
Additionally, an edge-case tie-breaker favored higher region affinity even when tier quota was zero, which allowed routes to burst pools without quota enforcement.
hotfixes_and_rollbacks: 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC: Rolled back fallback-selector refactor (reverted commit 9f2b3da) in control plane; stabilized routing decisions for hosted and dedicated customers.
2026-03-12 09:15 UTC: Applied patch to enforce quota check early in comparator (hotfix branch hotfix/ENG-4931-quota-check) to prevent burst pool routing without capacity.
2026-03-12 11:40 UTC: Deployed cache invalidation fix to compatibility matrix to ensure TTL <= 30s under churn (hotfix/compat-cache-ttl).
verification_steps: Smoke tests: end-to-end routing for 10k synthetic requests across three regions verifying correct model and tier assignment.
Audit query: no misroute events in production audit log for 2 hours post-deploy (query id: audit-20260312-EN4931).
Customer confirmation: engaged with two impacted customers; both validated restored behavior in Hosted and Dedicated within 3 hours of hotfix deployment.
postmortem_actions: 1) Rework comparator ordering so compatibility checks are decisive and always applied before region/tier heuristics (owner: Connor Liu).
2) Add unit + property tests for compatibility-cache churn and for tie-break scenarios (owner: María Gómez).
3) Instrument detailed metrics: compatibility-staleness, post-compare tie-break reasons, and quota-evaluation latency (owner: Priya Singh).
4) Create an emergency runbook for fallback-related regressions with steps to pin routing policies, rollback selector, and apply cache invalidation (owner: SRE team lead).
5) Add an integration test in CI that simulates Dedicated reserved pool exhaustion and verifies no automatic downgrade to burst without quota approval (owner: QA).
6) Schedule a design review for fallback policy semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to align product expectations (owner: PM - Rajiv Menon).
comments: 2026-03-12 03:20 - Rajiv Menon: Filed customer escalation with CSMs. Noting that Dedicated customers expect strict reserved-pool adherence; fallback should never violate lease semantics.
2026-03-12 04:05 - Connor Liu: Confirmed reproducible in staging; starting hotfix branch. Will revert selector patch and add early quota enforcement.
2026-03-12 08:45 - Aisha Patel: Rollback deployed to control plane (hosts cp-01/02). Early signs look stable; continuing validation.
2026-03-12 12:00 - María Gómez: Added property tests for compatibility-cache TTL; pushed to hotfix branch.
customer_notes: 2026-03-12 13:10 - CSM: Notified customers of mitigation and next steps; offering a post-incident call for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer A (FinTech): Confirmed latency and output quality returned to expected baseline after hotfix.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Customer B (Healthcare): Requested stronger guarantees for Private deployment route pinning -- escalated to PM Rajiv Menon.
next_steps: Merge tested comparator fix and cache invalidation into runtime-2.0.1 (target release 2026-03-16).
Complete postmortem doc and publish to incident channel; schedule follow-up design workshop (2026-03-19).
Implement CI integration test for dedicated-reserved semantics and run on every control-plane PR.
